title: Mosaic experiment docket — Jorge
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal ledger for a set of small inference experiments I ran while iterating on batching/quantization heuristics. Use this to snapshot numbers I care about, jot questions, and decide next small steps. Meant to be ephemeral; keep for 1–2 sprints then prune.

Context:
- Running subset of production traffic traces on local dev rig (4x A10G equivalent). Not representative of large fleet but useful for relative comparisons.
- Goal: find configuration that reduces per-token cost by >=20% while keeping subjective QA degradation <2 pts on fuzz QA score.

Quick CSV table (columns: date, exp_id, model, quant, batch, seq_len, tokens_run, p95_ms, throughput_tok/s, est_cost_per_1k_tokens_usd, qa_score_pct, notes):
2025-10-03, M-001, redwood/pythia-12b, fp16, 1, 512, 1.2k, 110, 180, 0.48, 94.2, baseline local: single request latency high but throughput stable
2025-10-07, M-002, redwood/pythia-12b, int8, 1, 512, 1.2k, 85, 230, 0.31, 92.6, int8 reduced latency/cost; slight QA drop; need eval on deterministic prompts
2025-10-11, M-003, redwood/pythia-12b, int8, 4, 512, 4.8k, 170, 540, 0.09, 92.4, batching x4 increases p95 due to queueing, but cost per token falls a lot
2025-10-15, M-004, open-llm/llama-13b, fp16, 1, 512, 1.3k, 130, 165, 0.52, 93.8, higher latency vs pythia-12b baseline here
2025-11-02, M-005, redwood/pythia-12b, int8, 2, 1024, 5.0k, 200, 600, 0.08, 92.0, longer seq increases memory pressure; check kv cache hit rate on real traffic
2025-11-20, M-006, redwood/pythia-12b, q4_0, 1, 512, 1.2k, 95, 210, 0.28, 91.5, q4_0 shows more quality regression; consider applying only to non-LLM-critical routes

Notes / internal observations:
- Int8 gave the best first-order savings with only ~1.6–2.7% QA drop. Worth trying canary on low-risk hosted routes.
- Batching helps cost but introduces larger tail latency. For interactive routes (chat streams) limit batch size to 2 or 4 depending on SLOs.
- q4_0 is promising for background jobs / rerankers but too lossy for generative-critical endpoints.
- Throughput_tok/s is noisy on dev rig; use median across 5 runs. Keep raw logs in /tmp/mosaic-runs/ for replay.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need a small A/B test on staging with 5% traffic to verify subjective QA delta. Create Linear ticket (RED-3124) — linked above.
- Try prefix caching combined with int8: run M-002 + prefix cache enabled, compare p95 and QA for templated prompts.
- Investigate memory allocation spikes on seq_len 1024 runs (seen on M-005). Possible kernel fallback on A10 drivers?

Quick to-do (next 2 weeks):
- [ ] Run M-002 + prefix cache (medium priority) — target date 2025-12-01
- [ ] Create canary config for hosted-api route chat-small with int8 (low risk) — draft config in gist and link in PR
- [ ] Export 50 sample responses from M-002 and M-001 and run pairwise blinded eval with PD team (Maya) — estimate 2 hours to set up

Scratch calculations (ballpark):
- cost per 1k tokens rough calc: (GPU $/hour) / (throughput_tok/s * 3600) * 1000 -> makes the estimates above (dev GPU costs tuned to $2.4/hr eq).
- p95 increases with batching roughly ~ baseline + 40ms * (batch_size - 1) (very rough on this rig).

Random quick notes to self:
- Save raw traces as gzipped jsonl with label exp_id for quick replays.
- If switching to Dedicated, check if autoscaler fragments batch windows (will change queuing behaviour).
- Keep this docket short-lived; move summary to shared drive doc if we decide to promote config.

End of docket.
summary: Personal one-page experiment ledger capturing small-batch quantization/batching runs, latencies, crude cost estimates, open questions, and next steps. For Jorge's quick iteration and handoff to Maya/Ethan if moving to canary.
